title: Development of an algae extract-based culture medium for Paenibacillus larvae without animal-derived components
author: Ryba, Píchová, et al.

steps.title: Weigh solid medium components
steps.instruction: Accurately weigh the solid ingredients for a 1 L batch: 20 g agar (2 % w/v), 10 g dried Chlorella algae extract (1 % w/v), 15 g yeast extract (powdered, bacteriology grade, 1.5 % w/v), 3 g potassium phosphate dibasic (K₂HPO₄, 0.3 % w/v), and 1 g sodium pyruvate (0.1 % w/v).

steps.title: Prepare 3 mM uric acid solution
steps.instruction: Weigh approximately 0.01 g uric acid (C₅H₄N₄O₃) and add to 20 mL distilled water. Gently heat to ~37 °C and/or add sterile 1 N NaOH dropwise while stirring until the uric acid is completely dissolved; monitor pH to avoid excessive alkalinity.

steps.title: Prepare 3 mM L‑tyrosine solution
steps.instruction: Weigh approximately 0.011 g L‑tyrosine and add to 20 mL distilled water (note low solubility in neutral water).

steps.title: Mix and autoclave basal medium
steps.instruction: In a autoclavable container with a capacity of at least 2 L, combine the weighed solid components with 920 mL distilled water, mix thoroughly, and autoclave at 121 °C for 15 min.

steps.title: Prepare sterile 10 % glucose solution
steps.instruction: Dissolve 2 g glucose in 18 mL distilled water to make a 10 % (w/v) solution, then sterilize by passing through a 0.22 µm filter into a sterile container.

steps.title: Add uric acid and L‑tyrosine solutions
steps.instruction: After autoclaving, cool the basal medium to 50–60 °C. Aseptically add the 20 mL uric acid solution. Warm the L‑tyrosine solution to 50–60 °C, stir until fully dissolved, and add it to the medium.

steps.title: Mix and pour agar plates
steps.instruction: Gently swirl the complete GPL medium to ensure uniform distribution. Under aseptic conditions, pour 15–20 mL into each sterile 90 mm Petri dish (≈3 mm depth). Allow plates to solidify at room temperature, then store inverted at 4 °C if not used immediately. One liter of medium yields approximately 50–67 plates.

steps.title: Inoculate P. larvae spores
steps.instruction: Spread Paenibacillus larvae spores onto GPL agar plates (and MYPGP control plates) and incubate at 35–37 °C for optimal spore germination.

steps.title: Visually assess colony growth
steps.instruction: After incubation, compare colony size, morphology, and density on GPL versus MYPGP plates; colonies should appear macroscopically identical, indicating equivalent support for germination and growth.

description: The efficacy of the newly developed GPL medium in supporting the germination and growth of P. larvae was validated by comparing its performance to that of the standard MYPGP medium. Spores of P. larvae were inoculated onto both MYPGP agar and GPL agar plates Fig. 1, which were prepared according to the method described above. The plates were incubated at optimal temperatures for spore germination (35–37 °C).Fig. 1Petri dish with GPL medium.Fig 1: Following incubation, the extent of P. larvae colony growth and morphology on both media types was visually assessed. The bacterial cultures appeared macroscopically identical in terms of colony size, morphology, and density, indicating that the GPL medium supports the germination and proliferation of P. larvae spores equally as well as the conventional MYPGP medium (Fig. 2).Fig. 2Paenibacillus larvae colony growth on a Petri dish containing GPL medium.Fig 2:
